pages.title: Missing Canonical Tag: Diagnosis and Repair
pages.direct_answer: An indexable HTML document returns no usable rel=canonical declaration in its raw or rendered head. To address missing canonical tag, emit one absolute, indexable, final-destination canonical from the server-rendered head. The acceptance condition is that raw and rendered HTML expose the same single canonical and the declared URL returns 200 without noindex.

evidence_artifact.label: Missing Canonical Tag: Diagnosis and Repair evidence fixture
evidence_artifact.description: Illustrative capture specification for missing canonical tag; not a live-client result.

diagnostic_procedure: Check whether an indexable HTML document returns no usable rel=canonical declaration in its raw or rendered head.
Capture the first response and each redirect hop; compare server and rendered output.
Inspect sitemap, canonical, and internal-link discovery for the affected URL.
Compare a passing template peer and record intended indexability before assigning impact.
pages.false_positive_boundary: A self-referencing canonical is recommended, but an absent tag is not automatically an error when every other signal is singular and stable.
repair_steps: Identify the authoritative route, content, or infrastructure owner.
Emit one absolute, indexable, final-destination canonical from the server-rendered head.
Regenerate affected links, metadata, structured data, and sitemaps.
Preserve the failure and a passing control as regression fixtures.
rerun_acceptance_check: Raw and rendered HTML expose the same single canonical and the declared URL returns 200 without noindex.
Repeated uncached captures agree on the repaired behavior.
The intended indexability and contextual discovery paths are preserved.

pages.title: Multiple Canonical Tags: Diagnosis and Repair

To address multiple canonical tags, assign one canonical owner and remove template, plugin, header, or client-side duplicates. The acceptance condition is that every delivery layer resolves to one normalized canonical target on two consecutive crawls.

To address canonical noindex conflict, choose index-and-consolidate or exclude, then remove the directive that contradicts that decision. The acceptance condition is that the final response has one coherent canonical/indexability state confirmed in headers and rendered HTML.

The acceptance condition is that removed URLs return the intended error status and retained URLs pass a rendered-content usefulness review.

pages.title: Robots-Blocked Indexable URL: Diagnosis and Repair
pages.direct_answer: Robots.txt prevents fetching a URL that remains discoverable and potentially indexable from external signals. To address robots blocked indexed page, remove an unintended block for a public page intended for search; for a page intended to leave search, instead permit the crawler to observe noindex or the removal status. The acceptance condition is that the crawler can fetch the response and observe the correct canonical and indexing directives for the documented publishing decision.
